ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High macro-level contrast; approximately 65-75% high-intensity white pixels centered in lobes against 25-35% low-intensity black pixels defining the borders and peduncle attachment.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Two large contiguous white (high-intensity) geometric blobs occupy the central regions of both lobes. These are bounded by thick black (low-intensity) margins along the trailing edges. A distinctive, wide black vertical band extends from the median notch area into the lower-middle section of the right lobe. Scattered dark pixel clusters (mottling) are visible in the lower interior of the left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 52 degrees and significant vertical depth relative to the fluke's horizontal plane.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular pixel-amplitude serrations (peaks and valleys) are concentrated on the distal half of the right lobe's trailing edge. The left lobe's trailing edge exhibits a smoother, lower-frequency undulation.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Sigmoid curvature; the trailing edge maintains a concave trajectory near the median notch, transitioning to a convex sweep toward the distal tips of both lobes.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Spatial detection of localized, roughly circular dark pixel clusters (mottling) on the interior white surface of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: The distal tip of the right lobe shows an irregular, ragged contour and potential blunting, indicating possible historical physical trauma or severe localized wear compared to the more tapered left tip.
other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced asymmetrical pigmentation intrusion at the median notch, where the black boundary extends significantly further into the right lobe's white field than it does on the left.
